text:
Four of six holes closed. The remaining two are split into P8.A5b (bd-01KYTXBANZN8X5NR5RTC39YHB1), not silently dropped.

CLOSED:
1. RelativeOutputPath now rejects "." segments as well as ".." (core/Workload.scala:13-24), so a/./b and a/b can no longer be distinct values naming one file and passing the string-equality duplicate checks in OutputManifest.from and DeclaredOutputs.from before colliding on write.
2. Process executors contain all non-fatal exceptions (local/Fs2CommandExecutor.scala:85, ssh/SshProcessRunner.scala:133). ProcessBuilder rejects invalid process values with unchecked exceptions — IllegalArgumentException, UnsupportedOperationException, NPE — which previously escaped InvocationResult as raised throwables. Now SpawnFailureKind.EnvironmentInvalid.
3. EventCursor.next and StoreRevision.next return Either and refuse to wrap (core/Identifiers.scala, managed/ManagedModel.scala), matching AttemptEpoch.next which already did it right. Threaded through ControlTransition.commit, which now returns Either and gained ControlFailure.JournalExhausted; ten Right(commit(...)) wrappers were unwrapped and one .map became .flatMap.
5. ContentDigest is structurally validated as sha256:<64 lowercase hex> (kernel/Identifiers.scala). It previously extended TextIdentifier and accepted "x".

DEFERRED to P8.A5b: private constructors for DurableResultHandle and TaskInvocation (three modules each, needs Either threaded through six sites including decoders), and splitting SiteToken into distinct site types (A5 itself ranked this last). ResultContractDescriptor WAS closed here — it had no callers outside core — with a validating `from` enforcing the mode/schema/outputs consistency its three producers already relied on.

Worth recording, because it is the strongest evidence the digest hole was real: tightening ContentDigest broke 16 test sites across 8 files, every one of them constructing a digest of the form "sha256:worker", "sha256:first", "sha256:remote-batch-suite" — plausible-looking labels that no hash function could ever produce. One was not a test fixture at all but the agent runtime config path (AgentStdioServerSuite passing "sha256:worker-v1" as WorkerReleaseDigestEnvironment, decoded by AgentMain.scala:169), so an operator could have configured a release digest that was not a digest.

These were replaced with real sha256 hashes of their own labels, computed with shasum, so each fixture stays traceable to its name. That is correcting invalid fixture data, not weakening a test: no assertion was relaxed and the tightened validation is exactly what caught them.

Verification: full suite 328, 0 failed. 3 new tests in core/InvariantClosureSuite covering path spelling, digest structure, and cursor overflow. scalafmt clean.
